decisions.reason: As a very recent launch in a narrow but strategic particle-therapy niche, management would likely tolerate early uncertainty and the delayed US rollout because it fits the firm's core dosimetry capabilities and there is not yet enough evidence of performance below aspiration to trigger withdrawal.

This chamber sits squarely in the firm's established measurement portfolio, so a behavioral-theory management would usually keep it on the market while learning from initial sales and customer use rather than abandoning it immediately.

Because it is closely related to existing competencies and likely part of a broader chamber family, the firm would view short-run results as still noisy and keep the product unless a clear aspiration shortfall emerged.

A standard clinical ionization chamber is highly consistent with the firm's mainstream business, making it likely that available organizational slack and service infrastructure support continued market presence.

Although relative dosimetry products can face specialist competition, the product is complementary to the firm's QA offering, so management would probably continue it while assessing adoption against internal aspirations and peer benchmarks.

A thimble ionization chamber is a core, credible extension of the firm's dosimetry line, and in the absence of visible failure the firm would be more likely to retain it than redeploy resources so soon after launch.
